_doc: cm#185 schema bring-forward manifest. Cross-checked against each file's own in-file header directive (first non-blank lines: '-- handoff:dialect postgres' | '-- handoff:dialect sqlite' | '-- handoff:excluded <reason>') by scripts/lib/schema-classify.js. This file provides CLASSIFICATION + EXPECTED-OBJECTS metadata only -- it is never the source of enumeration. Enumeration always reads the filesystem (scripts/sql/*.sql, non-recursive) and cross-checks git-tracked status; any enumerated file absent from this manifest, or any manifest entry whose classification disagrees with the file's own header directive, is a loud classification error (persistent project_settings 'schema_apply_degraded' row + stderr), never a silent skip. schema_epoch is a monotonically-bumped integer bumped whenever the applicable-unit set or any unit's DDL changes in a way that must force a re-apply on already-current databases; it is embedded as the '<epoch>:<hash>' prefix of the stored project_settings.schema_fingerprint value (see _computeSchemaFingerprint in scripts/handoff.js).

expected_objects._note: The pgvector-gated assertions.embedding column, assertions_embedding_hnsw_idx, and the pg_trgm-gated assertions_trgm_text_idx are deliberately EXCLUDED from this expected-objects list. Both DO $$ blocks that create them are designed to degrade gracefully (EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS) when the extension is absent -- the file's own header states 'no extensions, no halfvec, no pgvector dependency'. Including them here would convert an intentional optional degrade into a permanent stuck-degraded state on every stock Postgres instance without pgvector/pg_trgm installed. See PR body for the full rationale (S-13 scope interpretation).

pgvector_gated._doc: cm#224 follow-up (PR #225 independent review finding): declares the SAME excluded-from-expected_objects columns above so ensureSchemaCurrent's checkPgvectorGatedObjects (scripts/handoff.js) can detect, on every call, whether they were actually skipped on this DB -- a structured project_settings.schema_apply_degraded record + reason:'degraded' instead of a silent applied:true/reason:'current'. cm#185-schema-heal (adversary finding #6): 'type'/'dims' let checkPgvectorGatedObjects compare the column's ACTUAL pg_attribute/pg_type shape, not just its existence -- a hand-created assertions.embedding vector(1024) (this project's own prior legacy-1024-dim-store incident class) passes a bare existence probe but is not the halfvec(4000) column this engine's write path expects.

expected_fks._doc: FK follow-up to the schema-heal fingerprint fast path (PR #262): probeFastPathSchemaState verified column existence + pgvector shape but never the FK itself -- a column recreated without REFERENCES embedding_providers(id) reads HEALED and backfill-embeddings then fails at write time. table/columns/ref_table/ref_columns must each textually appear in this unit's own SQL (see ALTER TABLE assertions ADD COLUMN ... embedded_by_provider_id INTEGER REFERENCES embedding_providers(id)) -- enforced by schema-classify.js's manifest/DDL desync check.

expected_checks._doc: assertions.confidence CHECK (confidence >= 1.0 AND confidence <= 10.0). `def` is the FULL pg_get_constraintdef text (the CHECK(...) keyword included, byte-identical to a fresh throwaway DB's own rendering after applying this unit's SQL) -- healConstraints's ADD CONSTRAINT uses it AS-IS, never re-wrapped, so the same _normalizeDefText pipeline applies identically to both sides with no paren-layer mismatch.
assertions.suppression_kind CHECK (single authoritative block -- see suppression_kind CHECK comment in this unit's own SQL).
